summary: x87 assembler primitive (ABI lead names it x87_pow, LEGACY). Compares the absolute value of st0 with the extended-precision constant tbyte_5E6C0E and branches on the FPU status flags: if the compare flags are set, the value is tested against zero, producing +0.0 for zero and otherwise loading the constant tbyte_5E6BF0 (negated when the a1 flag is set); if the compare flags are clear, the value is rounded, fraction-isolated, and passed through f2xm1 (2^x - 1). Result is returned in st0.

operations.description: Duplicate st0, take its absolute value, load extended-precision constant tbyte_5E6C0E, compare both via fcompp, and store the FPU status word; branch on condition bits 0x41 (C0/C3)
On the compare-flags branch, test st0 against zero via ftst and store the status word
If st0 is zero, store byte value 4 at stack slot _EBP-144, pop st0, and load +0.0 via fldz as the result
Otherwise pop st0 and load the second extended-precision constant tbyte_5E6BF0; if the a1 flag is non-zero, negate it via fchs
On the non-compare branch, round st0 via frndint, exchange st(1)/st(0), subtract (fraction extraction), test/abs, then apply f2xm1 to compute 2^st0 - 1
Return the computed value in st0

unresolved: tbyte_5E6BF0 is referenced by the raw source but has no packet globals entry or evidence ref, so it is described but cannot be linked
The numerical values and meaning of the two extended-precision constants tbyte_5E6C0E / tbyte_5E6BF0 are unknown
Exact role of the a1 flag (conditional sign flip) is unproven
Caller/callee context is empty in this packet; the x87_pow ABI lead (LEGACY) is the only hint this is a power-function primitive
The stack byte 4 written to _EBP-144 is unexplained; it may be a status/tag write outside the visible frame
